# 1 Clement Chapter 37 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 1 Clement 37 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/1CL_037_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 37

**37:1** Let us therefore serve in the army as soldiers, brothers, with all earnestness under his faultless commands.

**37:2** Let us consider those who serve under our commanders, how orderly, how ready, how obediently they carry out commands.

**37:3** Not all are prefects nor tribunes nor centurions nor commanders of fifty and so on; but each one in his own rank carries out the orders of the king and the commanders.

**37:4** The great cannot exist without the small, nor the small without the great; there is a certain mixture among all things, and in this there is advantage.

**37:5** Let us take the body as an example. The head without the feet is nothing; and the feet without the head are nothing. The smallest members of the body are necessary and useful to the whole body. Indeed, all things breathe together and are united under a single subjection, toward the preservation of the whole body.

---

*EMET renders with maximal literalness. The military metaphor (vv. 1-3) and the body metaphor (vv. 4-5) are parallel arguments for ordered Christian community. The body image anticipates Paul (1 Cor 12:12-27) and may be influenced by the Roman Stoic tradition of the body politic.*
